decisions.justification: The first question offered aborting the whole run or skipping conflicting entries, and the user chose abort with no skipping or overwriting.
The first question asked whether to abort before changing anything, and the user later clarified that move-time failures must restore every original name.
The agent silently assumed exact `from === to` entries should be no-ops without asking whether already-conforming files belong in the rename set.
The agent decided to allow targets occupied by members of the moving source set through staging, but never put that policy to the user or ground it in a cited repository fact.
The user independently required that running the same command twice make the second run a no-op.
The user independently instructed, “Treat case-only clashes as clashes on this machine.”
The third question explicitly proposed clearly reporting rollback failures, and the user required identifying which files may need attention.
Neither participant settled whether preview or confirmation belonged in the fix or could be relied upon for safety.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr
mustAchieveMet: a run that cannot complete leaves every file unchanged
no existing file is ever overwritten

notes: The session correctly declared a bounded path, elicited the central collision policy, and adapted when the user identified the move-time atomicity gap. It implemented and tested staging, rollback, idempotency, case handling, and detailed failure reports, but silently chose self-inclusion and transient-collision semantics and never addressed the preview-mode decision.
